title: [YouPass Collect] - Trends in football match attendance in three European countries from 1980 to 2004
prompt: The graph below shows the average number of people attending top-level football matches in three European countries from 1980 to 2004. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates the average number of spectators attending top-tier football matches in Italy, England, and Germany over a 24-year period from 1980 to 2004.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, while attendance figures for Italy showed a general downward trend throughout the period, both England and Germany experienced overall increases, despite initial declines. Additionally, Italy had the highest attendance at the beginning but recorded the lowest figures by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: As for England and Germany, both started with similar attendance levels in 1980, at approximately 25,000 spectators in each country. England's figures then declined to their lowest point of around 22,000 in 1986, before beginning a steady recovery that accelerated significantly from 1998 onwards, ultimately reaching approximately 34,000 attendees by 2004. Germany followed a similar pattern, experiencing an even sharper initial drop to roughly 19,000 in 1986. However, the country subsequently witnessed a comparable upward trajectory, with attendance climbing back to about 23,000 in 1992, then matching England at 27,000 in 1998, before ending the period at approximately 33,000.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: In contrast, the figures for Italy moved in the opposite direction. Starting at 35,000 spectators in 1980, attendance in Italy peaked at around 37,000 in 1986. From this high point, however, attendance declined consistently throughout the remaining years, falling to 30,000 in 1992, then to 27,000 in 1998, and finally reaching approximately 25,000 by 2004.
